definitions.explanation: The way someone moves their hands when working with an object — a knife, cards, a tool, an instrument. Usually said admiringly of speed and precision.

examples.japanese: {見事|みごと}な{手|て}さばきだ。
{職人|しょくにん}の{手|て}さばきに{目|め}を{奪|うば}われた。
examples.english: I was captivated by the craftsman's handling.

examples.japanese: {板前|いたまえ}は{慣|な}れた{手|て}さばきで{魚|さかな}を{三枚|さんまい}におろした。
examples.english: With practiced hands the chef filleted the fish into three pieces.

notes:
{手|て} (hand) + さばき, the noun form of {捌|さば}く (to handle, to deal with). The word describes the visible motion of the hands, so it appears most often when someone is watching an expert at work.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鮮|あざ}やかな{手|て}さばき: brilliant handling
- {慣|な}れた{手|て}さばき: practiced, well-accustomed handling
- {手|て}さばきが{早|はや}い: to have quick hands

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手際|てぎわ}: skill, efficiency — covers the whole procedure, not just the hands
- {腕前|うでまえ}: ability, prowess — the level of skill itself rather than how it looks
